all_evidence.title: A systematic review of the evidence supporting post-operative antithrombotic use following cardiopulmonary bypass in children with CHD.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: Studies of warfarin and aspirin showed that laboratory monitoring levels were frequently out of therapeutic range (variably defined), and findings were mixed on the association of these derangements with bleeding or thrombotic events.
all_evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVES: To determine the optimal antithrombotic agent choice, timing of initiation, dosing and duration of therapy for paediatric patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. | METHODS: We used PubMed and EMBASE to systematically review the existing literature of clinical trials involving antithrombotics following cardiac surgery from 2000 to 2020 in children 0-18 years. | RESULTS: We identified 10 studies in 1929 children across three medications classes: vitamin K antagonists, cyclooxygenase inhibitors and indirect thrombin inhibitors.
all_evidence.key_finding: Studies of warfarin and aspirin showed that laboratory monitoring levels were frequently out of therapeutic range (variably defined), and findings were mixed on the association of these derangements with bleeding or thrombotic events.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 와파린과 아스피린은 검사 수치가 치료 범위를 벗어나는 일이 잦았는데, 그것이 출혈이나 혈전으로 이어지는지는 연구마다 엇갈렸습니다.
all_evidence.population: Studies of warfarin and aspirin showed that laboratory monitoring levels were frequently out of therapeutic range (variably defined), and findings were mixed on the association of these derangements with bleeding or thrombotic events. | Heparin was found to be safe at low doses, but breakthrough thromboembolic events were common.

all_evidence.title: Anticoagulants for people hospitalised with COVID-19: a rapid review.
all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_20: Higher-dose versus lower-dose anticoagulants (4 RCTs, 4647 participants) Higher-dose anticoagulants result in little or no difference in all-cause mortality (risk ratio (RR) 1.03, 95% CI 0.92 to 1.16, 4489 participants; 4 RCTs) and increase minor bleeding (RR 3.28, 95% CI 1.75 to 6.14, 1196 participants; 3 RCTs) compared to lower-dose anticoagulants up to 30 days (high-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: The primary manifestation of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is respiratory insufficiency that can also be related to diffuse pulmonary microthrombosis and thromboembolic events, such as pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, or arterial thrombosis. | People with COVID-19 who develop thromboembolism have a worse prognosis. | Anticoagulants such as heparinoids (heparins or pentasaccharides), vitamin K antagonists and direct anticoagulants are used for the prevention and treatment of venous or arterial thromboembolism.
all_evidence.key_finding: Higher-dose versus lower-dose anticoagulants (4 RCTs, 4647 participants) Higher-dose anticoagulants result in little or no difference in all-cause mortality (risk ratio (RR) 1.03, 95% CI 0.92 to 1.16, 4489 participants; 4 RCTs) and increase minor bleeding (RR 3.28, 95% CI 1.75 to 6.14, 1196 participants; 3 RCTs) compared to lower-dose anticoagulants up to 30 days (high-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 항응고제를 높은 용량으로 쓴 쪽은 낮은 용량과 견줘 사망 위험에 차이가 없었고, 가벼운 출혈만 늘었습니다(위험비 3.28).
all_evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't|Systematic Review
all_evidence.population: Anticoagulants such as heparinoids (heparins or pentasaccharides), vitamin K antagonists and direct anticoagulants are used for the prevention and treatment of venous or arterial thromboembolism. | Besides their anticoagulant properties, heparinoids have an additional anti-inflammatory potential. | However, the benefit of anticoagulants for people with COVID-19 is still under debate.

all_evidence.title: Efficacy and Safety of Direct Oral Anticoagulants in Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
all_evidence.venue: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_7: Compared with the standard of care, DOACs had non-significant reductions in the rates of major bleeding (1.2% vs 2.4%; RD = -1%, 95%CI: -6% to 3%), intracranial hemorrhage (1.9% vs 3.6%; RD = -2%, 95%CI:-7% to 3%), clinically relevant non-major bleeding (3.8% vs 7.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-9% to 2%), and any bleeding (17.3% vs 21.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-16% to 8%) in patients with CVT.
all_evidence.outcome: Current guidelines recommend the standard-of-care anticoagulation (vitamin K antagonists or low-molecular-weight heparin) in patients with cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT). | Herein, we performed a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) to assess the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) compared with the current standard of care in patients with CVT. | Compared with the standard of care, DOACs had non-significant reductions in the rates of major bleeding (1.2% vs 2.4%; RD = -1%, 95%CI: -6% to 3%), intracranial hemorrhage (1.9% vs 3.6%; RD = -2%, 95%CI:-7% to 3%), clinically relevant non-major bleeding (3.8% vs 7.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-9% to 2%), and any bleeding (17.3% vs 21.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-16% to 8%) in patients with CVT.
all_evidence.key_finding: Compared with the standard of care, DOACs had non-significant reductions in the rates of major bleeding (1.2% vs 2.4%; RD = -1%, 95%CI: -6% to 3%), intracranial hemorrhage (1.9% vs 3.6%; RD = -2%, 95%CI:-7% to 3%), clinically relevant non-major bleeding (3.8% vs 7.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-9% to 2%), and any bleeding (17.3% vs 21.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-16% to 8%) in patients with CVT.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 뇌정맥혈전증에서 직접작용 항응고제를 쓴 쪽의 큰 출혈이 1.2%, 표준 치료가 2.4% 로 줄었지만 통계로 뚜렷하지는 않았습니다.
all_evidence.population: Current guidelines recommend the standard-of-care anticoagulation (vitamin K antagonists or low-molecular-weight heparin) in patients with cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT). | Herein, we performed a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) to assess the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) compared with the current standard of care in patients with CVT.

all_evidence.title: Non-immunosuppressive treatment for IgA nephropathy.
all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_16: Compared to placebo or no treatment, renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibition probably decreases proteinuria (3 studies, 199 participants: MD - 0.71 g/24 h, 95% CI -1.04 to -0.39; moderate certainty evidence) but may result in little or no difference to kidney failure or doubling of serum creatinine (SCr), or complete remission of proteinuria (low certainty evidence).
all_evidence.outcome: We aimed to examine all non-immunosuppressive therapies (e.g. anticoagulants, antihypertensives, dietary restriction and supplementation, tonsillectomy, and herbal medicines) in the management of IgAN. | The risk of adverse events may be no different with RAS inhibition compared to either placebo or symptomatic treatment (low certainty evidence). | Anticoagulant therapy, fish oil, and traditional Chinese medicines exhibited small benefits to kidney function in patients with IgAN when compared to placebo or no treatment.
all_evidence.key_finding: Compared to placebo or no treatment, renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibition probably decreases proteinuria (3 studies, 199 participants: MD - 0.71 g/24 h, 95% CI -1.04 to -0.39; moderate certainty evidence) but may result in little or no difference to kidney failure or doubling of serum creatinine (SCr), or complete remission of proteinuria (low certainty evidence).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 레닌안지오텐신계 억제제를 쓴 쪽에서 단백뇨가 줄었지만(3개 연구, 199명), 신부전이나 혈청 크레아티닌 배가에서는 차이가 뚜렷하지 않았습니다.
all_evidence.population: We aimed to examine all non-immunosuppressive therapies (e.g. anticoagulants, antihypertensives, dietary restriction and supplementation, tonsillectomy, and herbal medicines) in the management of IgAN. | Anticoagulant therapy, fish oil, and traditional Chinese medicines exhibited small benefits to kidney function in patients with IgAN when compared to placebo or no treatment.

all_evidence.title: Safety and Efficacy of Non-Vitamin K Oral Anticoagulant Use Early After Cardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: Starting a NOAC on postoperative day 4 appeared to have similar bleeding rates compared with warfarin, but clinical application is limited by heterogeneity of outcome definitions, confounding, and bias.
all_evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVE: To determine the safety and efficacy of non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) initiated early after cardiac surgery. | STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Observational studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that initiated NOACs within the index hospitalization and that reported bleeding for the primary outcome were included. | Bleeding risk varied (0%-28.6%), and all but one study showed no significantly higher risk with NOAC compared with warfarin.
all_evidence.key_finding: Starting a NOAC on postoperative day 4 appeared to have similar bleeding rates compared with warfarin, but clinical application is limited by heterogeneity of outcome definitions, confounding, and bias.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 수술 나흘째부터 새 경구 항응고제를 시작해도 와파린과 출혈 발생이 비슷했지만, 연구마다 기준이 달라 그대로 적용하기는 어렵습니다.
all_evidence.population: OBJECTIVE: To determine the safety and efficacy of non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) initiated early after cardiac surgery. | Bleeding risk varied (0%-28.6%), and all but one study showed no significantly higher risk with NOAC compared with warfarin. | Starting a NOAC on postoperative day 4 appeared to have similar bleeding rates compared with warfarin, but clinical application is limited by heterogeneity of outcome definitions, confounding, and bias.

all_evidence.title: Fatal intracranial haemorrhage occurring after oral anticoagulant treatment initiation for secondary stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: CONCLUSIONS: Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants for intracranial haemorrhages and VKA-ICH occurring during secondary stroke prevention of AF patients have comparable baseline characteristics and outcomes except for the risk of fatal ICH within 30 days, which might be greater in VKA-ICH.
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: In this pooled analysis of seven multicentre cohorts potential differences were investigated in the incidence, characteristics and outcomes between intracranial haemorrhages (ICHs) associated with the use of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOAC-ICH) or with vitamin K antagonists (VKA-ICH) in ischaemic stroke patients after oral anticoagulant treatment initiation for atrial fibrillation (AF). | CONCLUSIONS: Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants for intracranial haemorrhages and VKA-ICH occurring during secondary stroke prevention of AF patients have comparable baseline characteristics and outcomes except for the risk of fatal ICH within 30 days, which might be greater in VKA-ICH.
all_evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSIONS: Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants for intracranial haemorrhages and VKA-ICH occurring during secondary stroke prevention of AF patients have comparable baseline characteristics and outcomes except for the risk of fatal ICH within 30 days, which might be greater in VKA-ICH.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 심방세동 환자의 뇌출혈에서 결과는 대체로 비슷했지만, 30일 안의 치명적 뇌출혈 위험은 비타민 K 길항제 쪽이 더 높을 수 있습니다.

all_evidence.title: Prediction of major and clinically relevant bleeding in patients with VTE treated with edoxaban or vitamin K antagonists.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: Significant risk factors for major bleeding during edoxaban treatment were female sex, concomitant antiplatelet therapy, haemoglobin ≤10 g/dl, history of arterial hypertension, and systolic blood pressure >160 mmHg.
all_evidence.outcome: Better understanding of risk factors for major bleeding events during anticoagulant treatment for venous thromboembolism (VTE) may help physicians when deciding on intensity and duration of treatment. | The primary aim of this study was to identify risk factors for major and clinically relevant bleeding in patients receiving the oral factor Xa inhibitor edoxaban or warfarin for the treatment of acute VTE. | Bleeding risk factors were evaluated in 4118 patients who received edoxaban and significant variables were combined in a prediction model.
all_evidence.key_finding: Significant risk factors for major bleeding during edoxaban treatment were female sex, concomitant antiplatelet therapy, haemoglobin ≤10 g/dl, history of arterial hypertension, and systolic blood pressure >160 mmHg.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 에독사반을 먹는 동안 큰 출혈 위험이 높았던 조건은 여성, 항혈소판제 병용, 헤모글로빈 10 g/dl 이하, 고혈압, 수축기혈압 160 초과였습니다.
all_evidence.publication_types: Clinical Trial, Phase III|Comparative Study|Journal Article|Multicenter Study|Randomized Controlled Trial|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
all_evidence.population: Better understanding of risk factors for major bleeding events during anticoagulant treatment for venous thromboembolism (VTE) may help physicians when deciding on intensity and duration of treatment. | The primary aim of this study was to identify risk factors for major and clinically relevant bleeding in patients receiving the oral factor Xa inhibitor edoxaban or warfarin for the treatment of acute VTE. | Major bleeding occurred in 56/4118 (1.4 %) patients given edoxaban and in 66/4122 (1.6 %) patients given warfarin.

all_evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants combined with antiplatelet drugs for patients with peripheral artery disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: Compared with antiplatelet drugs alone, NOACs combined with antiplatelet drugs resulted in lower risk of ischemic stroke events (OR = 0.75, 95%CI 0.57-0.98, p = 0.03), while other treatment effects were not worse than those of single antiplatelet drugs (p ≥ 0.05).
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: The efficacy and safety of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs) combined with antiplatelet drugs in patients with peripheral artery disease remain largely unknown. | OBJECTIVE: The aim of this meta-analysis was to explore the effects of NOACs combined with antiplatelet drugs versus antiplatelet drugs alone in this population. | According to the I2 statistic, a random or fixed-effect model was used to analyze the safety and effectiveness of NOACs combined with antiplatelet drugs in peripheral artery disease patients.
all_evidence.key_finding: Compared with antiplatelet drugs alone, NOACs combined with antiplatelet drugs resulted in lower risk of ischemic stroke events (OR = 0.75, 95%CI 0.57-0.98, p = 0.03), while other treatment effects were not worse than those of single antiplatelet drugs (p ≥ 0.05).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 항혈소판제만 쓴 쪽과 견줘 새 경구 항응고제를 같이 쓴 쪽의 허혈성 뇌졸중 위험이 낮았습니다(오즈비 0.75).
all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: The efficacy and safety of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs) combined with antiplatelet drugs in patients with peripheral artery disease remain largely unknown.

all_evidence.title: An Updated Meta-Analysis of DOACs vs. VKAs in Atrial Fibrillation Patients With Bioprosthetic Heart Valve.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: In terms of the safety outcomes, DOACs was associated with lower risks of major bleeding (RR = 0.70, 95%CI: 0.59-0.82) and intracranial bleeding (RR = 0.42, 95%CI: 0.26-0.70), but the risks of any bleeding (RR = 0.85, 95%CI: 0.65-1.13) and gastrointestinal bleeding (RR = 0.92, 95%CI: 0.73-1.17) are not significantly different when compared with VKAs.
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend the utilization of direct-acting oral anticoagulants (DOACs) in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (AF). | However, the optimal anticoagulation strategy for AF patients with bioprosthetic heart valves (BPHV) remains controversial. | In terms of the safety outcomes, DOACs was associated with lower risks of major bleeding (RR = 0.70, 95%CI: 0.59-0.82) and intracranial bleeding (RR = 0.42, 95%CI: 0.26-0.70), but the risks of any bleeding (RR = 0.85, 95%CI: 0.65-1.13) and gastrointestinal bleeding (RR = 0.92, 95%CI: 0.73-1.17) are not significantly different when compared with VKAs.
all_evidence.key_finding: In terms of the safety outcomes, DOACs was associated with lower risks of major bleeding (RR = 0.70, 95%CI: 0.59-0.82) and intracranial bleeding (RR = 0.42, 95%CI: 0.26-0.70), but the risks of any bleeding (RR = 0.85, 95%CI: 0.65-1.13) and gastrointestinal bleeding (RR = 0.92, 95%CI: 0.73-1.17) are not significantly different when compared with VKAs.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 직접작용 항응고제를 쓴 쪽에서 큰 출혈(0.70)과 뇌출혈(0.42) 위험이 낮았지만, 전체 출혈과 위장관 출혈은 차이가 없었습니다.

all_evidence.title: Management of thrombotic and obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome: a systematic literature review informing the EULAR recommendations for the management of antiphospholipid syndrome in adults.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: In individuals with high-risk antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) profile without prior thrombotic or obstetric APS, two meta-analyses showed a protective effect of low-dose aspirin (LDA) against thrombosis.
all_evidence.outcome: In individuals with high-risk antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) profile without prior thrombotic or obstetric APS, two meta-analyses showed a protective effect of low-dose aspirin (LDA) against thrombosis. | Two randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and three cohort studies showed no additional benefit of treatment with vitamin K antagonists at target international normalised ratio (INR) 3-4 versus INR 2-3 in patients with venous thrombosis. | In patients with arterial thrombosis, two RCTs and two cohort studies showed no difference in risk of recurrent thrombosis between the two target INR groups.
all_evidence.key_finding: In individuals with high-risk antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) profile without prior thrombotic or obstetric APS, two meta-analyses showed a protective effect of low-dose aspirin (LDA) against thrombosis.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 항인지질항체 위험도가 높은 사람에서 저용량 아스피린이 혈전을 막아 줬다는 메타분석이 두 편 있었습니다.
all_evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Meta-Analysis|Research Support, N.I.H., Intramural|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't|Systematic Review
all_evidence.population: One open-label trial showed higher rates of thrombosis recurrences in triple aPL-positive patients treated with rivaroxaban than those treated with warfarin. | RCTs and cohort studies showed that combination treatment with LDA and heparin was more effective than LDA alone in several types of obstetric APS.

all_evidence.title: Clinical safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of the novel factor Xa inhibitor DY-807f in healthy volunteers.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: RESULTS: DY-807f doses were safe and well-tolerated with no dose-dependent increase in adverse events up to 360 mg.
all_evidence.outcome: INTRODUCTION: Since Vitamin K antagonists are associated with various limitations such as narrow therapeutic window, slow onset and offset of effect, and numerous interactions with food and drugs, new oral anticoagulants targeted to inhibit thrombin or factor Xa (FXa) have been developed. | RESULTS: DY-807f doses were safe and well-tolerated with no dose-dependent increase in adverse events up to 360 mg. | Coagulation parameters (Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT) and Prothrombin Time (PT)) were linearly correlated with plasma DY-807 (free base of DY-807f) concentrations (correlation coefficient: 0.786 for aPTT, 0.945 for PT).
all_evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: DY-807f doses were safe and well-tolerated with no dose-dependent increase in adverse events up to 360 mg.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: DY-807f 는 360 mg 까지 용량을 올려도 이상반응이 늘지 않았고 잘 견뎠습니다.

all_evidence.title: Phase 1 study of the effect of icosapent ethyl on warfarin pharmacokinetic and anticoagulation parameters.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: CONCLUSIONS: IPE 4 g/day did not significantly change the single-dose AUC(0-∞) or C(max) of R- and S-warfarin or the anticoagulation pharmacodynamics of warfarin when co-administered as racemic warfarin at 25 mg.
all_evidence.outcome: EPA, the active metabolite of IPE, is mainly metabolized via β-oxidation, and studies suggest that omega-3 fatty acids such as EPA may have antithrombotic effects. | The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of IPE on the pharmacokinetic and anticoagulation pharmacodynamics of warfarin, a substrate of cytochrome P450 2C9-mediated metabolism. | Primary pharmacokinetic end points were area under the concentration-versus-time curve from zero to infinity (AUC(0-∞)) and maximum plasma concentration (C(max)) for R- and S-warfarin; pharmacodynamic end points were area under the international normalized ratio (INR) effect-time curve after the warfarin dose (AUC(INR)) and maximum INR (INR(max)).
all_evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSIONS: IPE 4 g/day did not significantly change the single-dose AUC(0-∞) or C(max) of R- and S-warfarin or the anticoagulation pharmacodynamics of warfarin when co-administered as racemic warfarin at 25 mg.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 이코사펜트에틸 4 g/day 를 와파린 25 mg 과 같이 먹었을 때 와파린 혈중 농도와 항응고 효과는 달라지지 않았습니다.
all_evidence.publication_types: Clinical Trial, Phase I|Journal Article|Randomized Controlled Trial|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
all_evidence.population: The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of IPE on the pharmacokinetic and anticoagulation pharmacodynamics of warfarin, a substrate of cytochrome P450 2C9-mediated metabolism. | METHODS: Healthy adults received oral warfarin (25 mg) on day 1, oral IPE (4 g/day) on days 8-35, and co-administration on Day 29. | Primary pharmacokinetic end points were area under the concentration-versus-time curve from zero to infinity (AUC(0-∞)) and maximum plasma concentration (C(max)) for R- and S-warfarin; pharmacodynamic end points were area under the international normalized ratio (INR) effect-time curve after the warfarin dose (AUC(INR)) and maximum INR (INR(max)).

evidence.title: Fixed- Versus Variable-Dose Prothrombin Complex Concentrate for the Emergent Reversal of Vitamin K Antagonists: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_12: CONCLUSIONS: A fixed-dose regimen for 4-PCC administration provides benefits over a variable-dose regimen in terms of dose reduction, faster administration time, improved clinical hemostasis, and reduced mortality and thromboembolic events.
evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVES: Four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4-PCC) is recommended for rapid reversal of vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) such as warfarin, yet optimal dosing remains uncertain. | Extracranial bleeding was the predominant indication, while intracranial hemorrhage varied. | While there is no clear difference between the two regimens in terms of achieving a goal international normalized ratio (INR) less than 2, a fixed-dose regimen is less likely to achieve a goal INR less than 1.5.
evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSIONS: A fixed-dose regimen for 4-PCC administration provides benefits over a variable-dose regimen in terms of dose reduction, faster administration time, improved clinical hemostasis, and reduced mortality and thromboembolic events.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 4인자 프로트롬빈 복합체를 정해진 용량으로 준 쪽이 몸무게에 맞춰 준 쪽보다 투여가 빨랐고 지혈이 나았으며 사망과 혈전 사건이 줄었습니다.
evidence.population: OBJECTIVES: Four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4-PCC) is recommended for rapid reversal of vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) such as warfarin, yet optimal dosing remains uncertain.

evidence.title: Deterioration of renal function is delayed in patients with atrial fibrillation treated with direct oral anticoagulants compared to vitamin K antagonists: systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_7: DOACs were associated with a lower risk of ≥30 % eGFR decline (HR:0.72, 95 %CI:0.59-0.88), progression to stage five CKD (HR:0.49,95 %CI:0.37-0.64) and doubling of serum creatinine (HR:0.50, 95 %CI:0.42-0.61). ≥30 % eGFR decline was also lower when apixaban, dabigatran and rivaroxaban were compared separately to VKAs, (HR:0.81, 95 %CI:0.69-0.95), (HR:0.61, 95 %CI:0.48-0.78) and (HR:0.80, 95 %CI:0.70-0.92) respectively.
evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: The use of anticoagulants has been linked to anticoagulant-related nephropathy, a condition initially reported in patients treated with warfarin. | However, cases have also been documented in patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs).
evidence.key_finding: DOACs were associated with a lower risk of ≥30 % eGFR decline (HR:0.72, 95 %CI:0.59-0.88), progression to stage five CKD (HR:0.49,95 %CI:0.37-0.64) and doubling of serum creatinine (HR:0.50, 95 %CI:0.42-0.61). ≥30 % eGFR decline was also lower when apixaban, dabigatran and rivaroxaban were compared separately to VKAs, (HR:0.81, 95 %CI:0.69-0.95), (HR:0.61, 95 %CI:0.48-0.78) and (HR:0.80, 95 %CI:0.70-0.92) respectively.

evidence.population: BACKGROUND: The use of anticoagulants has been linked to anticoagulant-related nephropathy, a condition initially reported in patients treated with warfarin. | However, cases have also been documented in patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). | DOACs were associated with a lower risk of ≥30 % eGFR decline (HR:0.72, 95 %CI:0.59-0.88), progression to stage five CKD (HR:0.49,95 %CI:0.37-0.64) and doubling of serum creatinine (HR:0.50, 95 %CI:0.42-0.61). ≥30 % eGFR decline was also lower when apixaban, dabigatran and rivaroxaban were compared separately to VKAs, (HR:0.81, 95 %CI:0.69-0.95), (HR:0.61, 95 %CI:0.48-0.78) and (HR:0.80, 95 %CI:0.70-0.92) respectively.

evidence.title: A systematic review of the evidence supporting post-operative antithrombotic use following cardiopulmonary bypass in children with CHD.
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: Studies of warfarin and aspirin showed that laboratory monitoring levels were frequently out of therapeutic range (variably defined), and findings were mixed on the association of these derangements with bleeding or thrombotic events.
evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVES: To determine the optimal antithrombotic agent choice, timing of initiation, dosing and duration of therapy for paediatric patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. | METHODS: We used PubMed and EMBASE to systematically review the existing literature of clinical trials involving antithrombotics following cardiac surgery from 2000 to 2020 in children 0-18 years. | RESULTS: We identified 10 studies in 1929 children across three medications classes: vitamin K antagonists, cyclooxygenase inhibitors and indirect thrombin inhibitors.
evidence.key_finding: Studies of warfarin and aspirin showed that laboratory monitoring levels were frequently out of therapeutic range (variably defined), and findings were mixed on the association of these derangements with bleeding or thrombotic events.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 와파린과 아스피린은 검사 수치가 치료 범위를 벗어나는 일이 잦았는데, 그것이 출혈이나 혈전으로 이어지는지는 연구마다 엇갈렸습니다.
evidence.population: Studies of warfarin and aspirin showed that laboratory monitoring levels were frequently out of therapeutic range (variably defined), and findings were mixed on the association of these derangements with bleeding or thrombotic events. | Heparin was found to be safe at low doses, but breakthrough thromboembolic events were common.

all_evidence.title: Anticoagulants for people hospitalised with COVID-19: a rapid review.
all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_20: Higher-dose versus lower-dose anticoagulants (4 RCTs, 4647 participants) Higher-dose anticoagulants result in little or no difference in all-cause mortality (risk ratio (RR) 1.03, 95% CI 0.92 to 1.16, 4489 participants; 4 RCTs) and increase minor bleeding (RR 3.28, 95% CI 1.75 to 6.14, 1196 participants; 3 RCTs) compared to lower-dose anticoagulants up to 30 days (high-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: The primary manifestation of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is respiratory insufficiency that can also be related to diffuse pulmonary microthrombosis and thromboembolic events, such as pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, or arterial thrombosis. | People with COVID-19 who develop thromboembolism have a worse prognosis. | Anticoagulants such as heparinoids (heparins or pentasaccharides), vitamin K antagonists and direct anticoagulants are used for the prevention and treatment of venous or arterial thromboembolism.
all_evidence.key_finding: Higher-dose versus lower-dose anticoagulants (4 RCTs, 4647 participants) Higher-dose anticoagulants result in little or no difference in all-cause mortality (risk ratio (RR) 1.03, 95% CI 0.92 to 1.16, 4489 participants; 4 RCTs) and increase minor bleeding (RR 3.28, 95% CI 1.75 to 6.14, 1196 participants; 3 RCTs) compared to lower-dose anticoagulants up to 30 days (high-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 항응고제를 높은 용량으로 쓴 쪽은 낮은 용량과 견줘 사망 위험에 차이가 없었고, 가벼운 출혈만 늘었습니다(위험비 3.28).
all_evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't|Systematic Review
all_evidence.population: Anticoagulants such as heparinoids (heparins or pentasaccharides), vitamin K antagonists and direct anticoagulants are used for the prevention and treatment of venous or arterial thromboembolism. | Besides their anticoagulant properties, heparinoids have an additional anti-inflammatory potential. | However, the benefit of anticoagulants for people with COVID-19 is still under debate.

all_evidence.title: Non-immunosuppressive treatment for IgA nephropathy.
all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_16: Compared to placebo or no treatment, renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibition probably decreases proteinuria (3 studies, 199 participants: MD - 0.71 g/24 h, 95% CI -1.04 to -0.39; moderate certainty evidence) but may result in little or no difference to kidney failure or doubling of serum creatinine (SCr), or complete remission of proteinuria (low certainty evidence).
all_evidence.outcome: We aimed to examine all non-immunosuppressive therapies (e.g. anticoagulants, antihypertensives, dietary restriction and supplementation, tonsillectomy, and herbal medicines) in the management of IgAN. | The risk of adverse events may be no different with RAS inhibition compared to either placebo or symptomatic treatment (low certainty evidence). | Anticoagulant therapy, fish oil, and traditional Chinese medicines exhibited small benefits to kidney function in patients with IgAN when compared to placebo or no treatment.

evidence.title: Fixed- Versus Variable-Dose Prothrombin Complex Concentrate for the Emergent Reversal of Vitamin K Antagonists: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_12: CONCLUSIONS: A fixed-dose regimen for 4-PCC administration provides benefits over a variable-dose regimen in terms of dose reduction, faster administration time, improved clinical hemostasis, and reduced mortality and thromboembolic events.
evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVES: Four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4-PCC) is recommended for rapid reversal of vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) such as warfarin, yet optimal dosing remains uncertain. | Extracranial bleeding was the predominant indication, while intracranial hemorrhage varied. | While there is no clear difference between the two regimens in terms of achieving a goal international normalized ratio (INR) less than 2, a fixed-dose regimen is less likely to achieve a goal INR less than 1.5.
evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSIONS: A fixed-dose regimen for 4-PCC administration provides benefits over a variable-dose regimen in terms of dose reduction, faster administration time, improved clinical hemostasis, and reduced mortality and thromboembolic events.

evidence.title: Direct Oral Anticoagulants versus Vitamin K Antagonists for Left Ventricular Thrombus: A Meta-Analysis with Trial Sequential Analysis.
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_7: There was no significant difference between groups for stroke or systemic embolic (SSE) events (RR 0.84; 95% CI 0.65 to 1.07; p = 0.157), stroke (RR 0.73; 95% CI 0.48 to 1.11; p = 0.140), systemic embolic (SE) events (RR 0.69; 95% CI 0.40 to 1.17; p = 0.166), thrombus resolution (RR 1.05; 95% CI 0.99 to 1.11; p = 0.077), any bleeding (RR 0.78; 95% CI 0.60 to 1.00; p = 0.054), clinically relevant bleeding (RR 0.69; 95% CI 0.46 to 1.03; p = 0.066), minor bleeding (RR 0.73; 95% CI 0.43 to 1.23; p = 0.234), major bleeding (RR 0.87; 95% CI 0.42 to 1.80; p = 0.705), and all-cause mortality (RR 1.05; 95% CI 0.79 to 1.39; p = 0.752).
evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) are the recommended first-line treatment for left ventricular thrombus (LVT); however, direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have been considered an alternative therapy. | There was no significant difference between groups for stroke or systemic embolic (SSE) events (RR 0.84; 95% CI 0.65 to 1.07; p = 0.157), stroke (RR 0.73; 95% CI 0.48 to 1.11; p = 0.140), systemic embolic (SE) events (RR 0.69; 95% CI 0.40 to 1.17; p = 0.166), thrombus resolution (RR 1.05; 95% CI 0.99 to 1.11; p = 0.077), any bleeding (RR 0.78; 95% CI 0.60 to 1.00; p = 0.054), clinically relevant bleeding (RR 0.69; 95% CI 0.46 to 1.03; p = 0.066), minor bleeding (RR 0.73; 95% CI 0.43 to 1.23; p = 0.234), major bleeding (RR 0.87; 95% CI 0.42 to 1.80; p = 0.705), and all-cause mortality (RR 1.05; 95% CI 0.79 to 1.39; p = 0.752). | CONCLUSIONS: DOACs had a similar rate of thromboembolic and hemorrhagic events, as well as thrombus resolution, compared to VKAs in the treatment of LVTs.
evidence.key_finding: There was no significant difference between groups for stroke or systemic embolic (SSE) events (RR 0.84; 95% CI 0.65 to 1.07; p = 0.157), stroke (RR 0.73; 95% CI 0.48 to 1.11; p = 0.140), systemic embolic (SE) events (RR 0.69; 95% CI 0.40 to 1.17; p = 0.166), thrombus resolution (RR 1.05; 95% CI 0.99 to 1.11; p = 0.077), any bleeding (RR 0.78; 95% CI 0.60 to 1.00; p = 0.054), clinically relevant bleeding (RR 0.69; 95% CI 0.46 to 1.03; p = 0.066), minor bleeding (RR 0.73; 95% CI 0.43 to 1.23; p = 0.234), major bleeding (RR 0.87; 95% CI 0.42 to 1.80; p = 0.705), and all-cause mortality (RR 1.05; 95% CI 0.79 to 1.39; p = 0.752).
evidence.key_finding_ko: 여러 결과를 봤지만 뇌졸중, 색전증, 출혈, 사망 위험 어디에서도 뚜렷한 차이가 없었습니다.
evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) are the recommended first-line treatment for left ventricular thrombus (LVT); however, direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have been considered an alternative therapy. | Compared with VKAs, rivaroxaban significantly reduced SSE events (RR 0.35; 95% CI 0.16 to 0.91; p = 0.029) and SE events (RR 0.39; 95% CI 0.16 to 0.95; p = 0.037). | Rivaroxaban therapy had a significant reduction in thromboembolic events, compared to VKAs.

evidence.title: Deterioration of renal function is delayed in patients with atrial fibrillation treated with direct oral anticoagulants compared to vitamin K antagonists: systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_7: DOACs were associated with a lower risk of ≥30 % eGFR decline (HR:0.72, 95 %CI:0.59-0.88), progression to stage five CKD (HR:0.49,95 %CI:0.37-0.64) and doubling of serum creatinine (HR:0.50, 95 %CI:0.42-0.61). ≥30 % eGFR decline was also lower when apixaban, dabigatran and rivaroxaban were compared separately to VKAs, (HR:0.81, 95 %CI:0.69-0.95), (HR:0.61, 95 %CI:0.48-0.78) and (HR:0.80, 95 %CI:0.70-0.92) respectively.
evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: The use of anticoagulants has been linked to anticoagulant-related nephropathy, a condition initially reported in patients treated with warfarin. | However, cases have also been documented in patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs).
evidence.key_finding: DOACs were associated with a lower risk of ≥30 % eGFR decline (HR:0.72, 95 %CI:0.59-0.88), progression to stage five CKD (HR:0.49,95 %CI:0.37-0.64) and doubling of serum creatinine (HR:0.50, 95 %CI:0.42-0.61). ≥30 % eGFR decline was also lower when apixaban, dabigatran and rivaroxaban were compared separately to VKAs, (HR:0.81, 95 %CI:0.69-0.95), (HR:0.61, 95 %CI:0.48-0.78) and (HR:0.80, 95 %CI:0.70-0.92) respectively.

all_evidence.title: A systematic review of the evidence supporting post-operative antithrombotic use following cardiopulmonary bypass in children with CHD.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: Studies of warfarin and aspirin showed that laboratory monitoring levels were frequently out of therapeutic range (variably defined), and findings were mixed on the association of these derangements with bleeding or thrombotic events.
all_evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVES: To determine the optimal antithrombotic agent choice, timing of initiation, dosing and duration of therapy for paediatric patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. | METHODS: We used PubMed and EMBASE to systematically review the existing literature of clinical trials involving antithrombotics following cardiac surgery from 2000 to 2020 in children 0-18 years. | RESULTS: We identified 10 studies in 1929 children across three medications classes: vitamin K antagonists, cyclooxygenase inhibitors and indirect thrombin inhibitors.
all_evidence.key_finding: Studies of warfarin and aspirin showed that laboratory monitoring levels were frequently out of therapeutic range (variably defined), and findings were mixed on the association of these derangements with bleeding or thrombotic events.

all_evidence.title: Anticoagulants for people hospitalised with COVID-19: a rapid review.
all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_20: Higher-dose versus lower-dose anticoagulants (4 RCTs, 4647 participants) Higher-dose anticoagulants result in little or no difference in all-cause mortality (risk ratio (RR) 1.03, 95% CI 0.92 to 1.16, 4489 participants; 4 RCTs) and increase minor bleeding (RR 3.28, 95% CI 1.75 to 6.14, 1196 participants; 3 RCTs) compared to lower-dose anticoagulants up to 30 days (high-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: The primary manifestation of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is respiratory insufficiency that can also be related to diffuse pulmonary microthrombosis and thromboembolic events, such as pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, or arterial thrombosis. | People with COVID-19 who develop thromboembolism have a worse prognosis. | Anticoagulants such as heparinoids (heparins or pentasaccharides), vitamin K antagonists and direct anticoagulants are used for the prevention and treatment of venous or arterial thromboembolism.
all_evidence.key_finding: Higher-dose versus lower-dose anticoagulants (4 RCTs, 4647 participants) Higher-dose anticoagulants result in little or no difference in all-cause mortality (risk ratio (RR) 1.03, 95% CI 0.92 to 1.16, 4489 participants; 4 RCTs) and increase minor bleeding (RR 3.28, 95% CI 1.75 to 6.14, 1196 participants; 3 RCTs) compared to lower-dose anticoagulants up to 30 days (high-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 항응고제를 높은 용량으로 쓴 쪽은 낮은 용량과 견줘 사망 위험에 차이가 없었고, 가벼운 출혈만 늘었습니다(위험비 3.28).

all_evidence.title: Efficacy and Safety of Direct Oral Anticoagulants in Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
all_evidence.venue: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_7: Compared with the standard of care, DOACs had non-significant reductions in the rates of major bleeding (1.2% vs 2.4%; RD = -1%, 95%CI: -6% to 3%), intracranial hemorrhage (1.9% vs 3.6%; RD = -2%, 95%CI:-7% to 3%), clinically relevant non-major bleeding (3.8% vs 7.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-9% to 2%), and any bleeding (17.3% vs 21.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-16% to 8%) in patients with CVT.
all_evidence.outcome: Current guidelines recommend the standard-of-care anticoagulation (vitamin K antagonists or low-molecular-weight heparin) in patients with cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT). | Herein, we performed a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) to assess the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) compared with the current standard of care in patients with CVT. | Compared with the standard of care, DOACs had non-significant reductions in the rates of major bleeding (1.2% vs 2.4%; RD = -1%, 95%CI: -6% to 3%), intracranial hemorrhage (1.9% vs 3.6%; RD = -2%, 95%CI:-7% to 3%), clinically relevant non-major bleeding (3.8% vs 7.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-9% to 2%), and any bleeding (17.3% vs 21.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-16% to 8%) in patients with CVT.
all_evidence.key_finding: Compared with the standard of care, DOACs had non-significant reductions in the rates of major bleeding (1.2% vs 2.4%; RD = -1%, 95%CI: -6% to 3%), intracranial hemorrhage (1.9% vs 3.6%; RD = -2%, 95%CI:-7% to 3%), clinically relevant non-major bleeding (3.8% vs 7.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-9% to 2%), and any bleeding (17.3% vs 21.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-16% to 8%) in patients with CVT.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 뇌정맥혈전증에서 직접작용 항응고제를 쓴 쪽의 큰 출혈이 1.2%, 표준 치료가 2.4% 로 줄었지만 통계로 뚜렷하지는 않았습니다.
all_evidence.population: Current guidelines recommend the standard-of-care anticoagulation (vitamin K antagonists or low-molecular-weight heparin) in patients with cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT). | Herein, we performed a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) to assess the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) compared with the current standard of care in patients with CVT.

all_evidence.title: Non-immunosuppressive treatment for IgA nephropathy.
all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_16: Compared to placebo or no treatment, renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibition probably decreases proteinuria (3 studies, 199 participants: MD - 0.71 g/24 h, 95% CI -1.04 to -0.39; moderate certainty evidence) but may result in little or no difference to kidney failure or doubling of serum creatinine (SCr), or complete remission of proteinuria (low certainty evidence).
all_evidence.outcome: We aimed to examine all non-immunosuppressive therapies (e.g. anticoagulants, antihypertensives, dietary restriction and supplementation, tonsillectomy, and herbal medicines) in the management of IgAN. | The risk of adverse events may be no different with RAS inhibition compared to either placebo or symptomatic treatment (low certainty evidence). | Anticoagulant therapy, fish oil, and traditional Chinese medicines exhibited small benefits to kidney function in patients with IgAN when compared to placebo or no treatment.
all_evidence.key_finding: Compared to placebo or no treatment, renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibition probably decreases proteinuria (3 studies, 199 participants: MD - 0.71 g/24 h, 95% CI -1.04 to -0.39; moderate certainty evidence) but may result in little or no difference to kidney failure or doubling of serum creatinine (SCr), or complete remission of proteinuria (low certainty evidence).

all_evidence.title: Safety and Efficacy of Non-Vitamin K Oral Anticoagulant Use Early After Cardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: Starting a NOAC on postoperative day 4 appeared to have similar bleeding rates compared with warfarin, but clinical application is limited by heterogeneity of outcome definitions, confounding, and bias.
all_evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVE: To determine the safety and efficacy of non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) initiated early after cardiac surgery. | STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Observational studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that initiated NOACs within the index hospitalization and that reported bleeding for the primary outcome were included. | Bleeding risk varied (0%-28.6%), and all but one study showed no significantly higher risk with NOAC compared with warfarin.
all_evidence.key_finding: Starting a NOAC on postoperative day 4 appeared to have similar bleeding rates compared with warfarin, but clinical application is limited by heterogeneity of outcome definitions, confounding, and bias.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 수술 나흘째부터 새 경구 항응고제를 시작해도 와파린과 출혈 발생이 비슷했지만, 연구마다 기준이 달라 그대로 적용하기는 어렵습니다.

all_evidence.title: Fatal intracranial haemorrhage occurring after oral anticoagulant treatment initiation for secondary stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: CONCLUSIONS: Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants for intracranial haemorrhages and VKA-ICH occurring during secondary stroke prevention of AF patients have comparable baseline characteristics and outcomes except for the risk of fatal ICH within 30 days, which might be greater in VKA-ICH.
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: In this pooled analysis of seven multicentre cohorts potential differences were investigated in the incidence, characteristics and outcomes between intracranial haemorrhages (ICHs) associated with the use of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOAC-ICH) or with vitamin K antagonists (VKA-ICH) in ischaemic stroke patients after oral anticoagulant treatment initiation for atrial fibrillation (AF). | CONCLUSIONS: Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants for intracranial haemorrhages and VKA-ICH occurring during secondary stroke prevention of AF patients have comparable baseline characteristics and outcomes except for the risk of fatal ICH within 30 days, which might be greater in VKA-ICH.
all_evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSIONS: Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants for intracranial haemorrhages and VKA-ICH occurring during secondary stroke prevention of AF patients have comparable baseline characteristics and outcomes except for the risk of fatal ICH within 30 days, which might be greater in VKA-ICH.

all_evidence.title: Prediction of major and clinically relevant bleeding in patients with VTE treated with edoxaban or vitamin K antagonists.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: Significant risk factors for major bleeding during edoxaban treatment were female sex, concomitant antiplatelet therapy, haemoglobin ≤10 g/dl, history of arterial hypertension, and systolic blood pressure >160 mmHg.
all_evidence.outcome: Better understanding of risk factors for major bleeding events during anticoagulant treatment for venous thromboembolism (VTE) may help physicians when deciding on intensity and duration of treatment. | The primary aim of this study was to identify risk factors for major and clinically relevant bleeding in patients receiving the oral factor Xa inhibitor edoxaban or warfarin for the treatment of acute VTE. | Bleeding risk factors were evaluated in 4118 patients who received edoxaban and significant variables were combined in a prediction model.
all_evidence.key_finding: Significant risk factors for major bleeding during edoxaban treatment were female sex, concomitant antiplatelet therapy, haemoglobin ≤10 g/dl, history of arterial hypertension, and systolic blood pressure >160 mmHg.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 에독사반을 먹는 동안 큰 출혈 위험이 높았던 조건은 여성, 항혈소판제 병용, 헤모글로빈 10 g/dl 이하, 고혈압, 수축기혈압 160 초과였습니다.
all_evidence.publication_types: Clinical Trial, Phase III|Comparative Study|Journal Article|Multicenter Study|Randomized Controlled Trial|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

all_evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants combined with antiplatelet drugs for patients with peripheral artery disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: Compared with antiplatelet drugs alone, NOACs combined with antiplatelet drugs resulted in lower risk of ischemic stroke events (OR = 0.75, 95%CI 0.57-0.98, p = 0.03), while other treatment effects were not worse than those of single antiplatelet drugs (p ≥ 0.05).
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: The efficacy and safety of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs) combined with antiplatelet drugs in patients with peripheral artery disease remain largely unknown. | OBJECTIVE: The aim of this meta-analysis was to explore the effects of NOACs combined with antiplatelet drugs versus antiplatelet drugs alone in this population. | According to the I2 statistic, a random or fixed-effect model was used to analyze the safety and effectiveness of NOACs combined with antiplatelet drugs in peripheral artery disease patients.
all_evidence.key_finding: Compared with antiplatelet drugs alone, NOACs combined with antiplatelet drugs resulted in lower risk of ischemic stroke events (OR = 0.75, 95%CI 0.57-0.98, p = 0.03), while other treatment effects were not worse than those of single antiplatelet drugs (p ≥ 0.05).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 항혈소판제만 쓴 쪽과 견줘 새 경구 항응고제를 같이 쓴 쪽의 허혈성 뇌졸중 위험이 낮았습니다(오즈비 0.75).

all_evidence.title: An Updated Meta-Analysis of DOACs vs. VKAs in Atrial Fibrillation Patients With Bioprosthetic Heart Valve.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: In terms of the safety outcomes, DOACs was associated with lower risks of major bleeding (RR = 0.70, 95%CI: 0.59-0.82) and intracranial bleeding (RR = 0.42, 95%CI: 0.26-0.70), but the risks of any bleeding (RR = 0.85, 95%CI: 0.65-1.13) and gastrointestinal bleeding (RR = 0.92, 95%CI: 0.73-1.17) are not significantly different when compared with VKAs.
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend the utilization of direct-acting oral anticoagulants (DOACs) in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (AF). | However, the optimal anticoagulation strategy for AF patients with bioprosthetic heart valves (BPHV) remains controversial. | In terms of the safety outcomes, DOACs was associated with lower risks of major bleeding (RR = 0.70, 95%CI: 0.59-0.82) and intracranial bleeding (RR = 0.42, 95%CI: 0.26-0.70), but the risks of any bleeding (RR = 0.85, 95%CI: 0.65-1.13) and gastrointestinal bleeding (RR = 0.92, 95%CI: 0.73-1.17) are not significantly different when compared with VKAs.
all_evidence.key_finding: In terms of the safety outcomes, DOACs was associated with lower risks of major bleeding (RR = 0.70, 95%CI: 0.59-0.82) and intracranial bleeding (RR = 0.42, 95%CI: 0.26-0.70), but the risks of any bleeding (RR = 0.85, 95%CI: 0.65-1.13) and gastrointestinal bleeding (RR = 0.92, 95%CI: 0.73-1.17) are not significantly different when compared with VKAs.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 직접작용 항응고제를 쓴 쪽에서 큰 출혈(0.70)과 뇌출혈(0.42) 위험이 낮았지만, 전체 출혈과 위장관 출혈은 차이가 없었습니다.

all_evidence.title: Management of thrombotic and obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome: a systematic literature review informing the EULAR recommendations for the management of antiphospholipid syndrome in adults.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: In individuals with high-risk antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) profile without prior thrombotic or obstetric APS, two meta-analyses showed a protective effect of low-dose aspirin (LDA) against thrombosis.
all_evidence.outcome: In individuals with high-risk antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) profile without prior thrombotic or obstetric APS, two meta-analyses showed a protective effect of low-dose aspirin (LDA) against thrombosis. | Two randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and three cohort studies showed no additional benefit of treatment with vitamin K antagonists at target international normalised ratio (INR) 3-4 versus INR 2-3 in patients with venous thrombosis. | In patients with arterial thrombosis, two RCTs and two cohort studies showed no difference in risk of recurrent thrombosis between the two target INR groups.
all_evidence.key_finding: In individuals with high-risk antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) profile without prior thrombotic or obstetric APS, two meta-analyses showed a protective effect of low-dose aspirin (LDA) against thrombosis.

all_evidence.title: Clinical safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of the novel factor Xa inhibitor DY-807f in healthy volunteers.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: RESULTS: DY-807f doses were safe and well-tolerated with no dose-dependent increase in adverse events up to 360 mg.
all_evidence.outcome: INTRODUCTION: Since Vitamin K antagonists are associated with various limitations such as narrow therapeutic window, slow onset and offset of effect, and numerous interactions with food and drugs, new oral anticoagulants targeted to inhibit thrombin or factor Xa (FXa) have been developed. | RESULTS: DY-807f doses were safe and well-tolerated with no dose-dependent increase in adverse events up to 360 mg. | Coagulation parameters (Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT) and Prothrombin Time (PT)) were linearly correlated with plasma DY-807 (free base of DY-807f) concentrations (correlation coefficient: 0.786 for aPTT, 0.945 for PT).
all_evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: DY-807f doses were safe and well-tolerated with no dose-dependent increase in adverse events up to 360 mg.

all_evidence.title: Phase 1 study of the effect of icosapent ethyl on warfarin pharmacokinetic and anticoagulation parameters.

all_evidence.outcome: EPA, the active metabolite of IPE, is mainly metabolized via β-oxidation, and studies suggest that omega-3 fatty acids such as EPA may have antithrombotic effects. | The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of IPE on the pharmacokinetic and anticoagulation pharmacodynamics of warfarin, a substrate of cytochrome P450 2C9-mediated metabolism. | Primary pharmacokinetic end points were area under the concentration-versus-time curve from zero to infinity (AUC(0-∞)) and maximum plasma concentration (C(max)) for R- and S-warfarin; pharmacodynamic end points were area under the international normalized ratio (INR) effect-time curve after the warfarin dose (AUC(INR)) and maximum INR (INR(max)).
all_evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSIONS: IPE 4 g/day did not significantly change the single-dose AUC(0-∞) or C(max) of R- and S-warfarin or the anticoagulation pharmacodynamics of warfarin when co-administered as racemic warfarin at 25 mg.

evidence.title: Deterioration of renal function is delayed in patients with atrial fibrillation treated with direct oral anticoagulants compared to vitamin K antagonists: systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_7: DOACs were associated with a lower risk of ≥30 % eGFR decline (HR:0.72, 95 %CI:0.59-0.88), progression to stage five CKD (HR:0.49,95 %CI:0.37-0.64) and doubling of serum creatinine (HR:0.50, 95 %CI:0.42-0.61). ≥30 % eGFR decline was also lower when apixaban, dabigatran and rivaroxaban were compared separately to VKAs, (HR:0.81, 95 %CI:0.69-0.95), (HR:0.61, 95 %CI:0.48-0.78) and (HR:0.80, 95 %CI:0.70-0.92) respectively.
evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: The use of anticoagulants has been linked to anticoagulant-related nephropathy, a condition initially reported in patients treated with warfarin. | However, cases have also been documented in patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs).
evidence.key_finding: DOACs were associated with a lower risk of ≥30 % eGFR decline (HR:0.72, 95 %CI:0.59-0.88), progression to stage five CKD (HR:0.49,95 %CI:0.37-0.64) and doubling of serum creatinine (HR:0.50, 95 %CI:0.42-0.61). ≥30 % eGFR decline was also lower when apixaban, dabigatran and rivaroxaban were compared separately to VKAs, (HR:0.81, 95 %CI:0.69-0.95), (HR:0.61, 95 %CI:0.48-0.78) and (HR:0.80, 95 %CI:0.70-0.92) respectively.

evidence.title: Efficacy and Safety of Direct Oral Anticoagulants in Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
evidence.venue: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_7: Compared with the standard of care, DOACs had non-significant reductions in the rates of major bleeding (1.2% vs 2.4%; RD = -1%, 95%CI: -6% to 3%), intracranial hemorrhage (1.9% vs 3.6%; RD = -2%, 95%CI:-7% to 3%), clinically relevant non-major bleeding (3.8% vs 7.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-9% to 2%), and any bleeding (17.3% vs 21.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-16% to 8%) in patients with CVT.
evidence.outcome: Current guidelines recommend the standard-of-care anticoagulation (vitamin K antagonists or low-molecular-weight heparin) in patients with cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT). | Herein, we performed a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) to assess the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) compared with the current standard of care in patients with CVT. | Compared with the standard of care, DOACs had non-significant reductions in the rates of major bleeding (1.2% vs 2.4%; RD = -1%, 95%CI: -6% to 3%), intracranial hemorrhage (1.9% vs 3.6%; RD = -2%, 95%CI:-7% to 3%), clinically relevant non-major bleeding (3.8% vs 7.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-9% to 2%), and any bleeding (17.3% vs 21.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-16% to 8%) in patients with CVT.
evidence.key_finding: Compared with the standard of care, DOACs had non-significant reductions in the rates of major bleeding (1.2% vs 2.4%; RD = -1%, 95%CI: -6% to 3%), intracranial hemorrhage (1.9% vs 3.6%; RD = -2%, 95%CI:-7% to 3%), clinically relevant non-major bleeding (3.8% vs 7.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-9% to 2%), and any bleeding (17.3% vs 21.4%; RD = -4%, 95%CI:-16% to 8%) in patients with CVT.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 뇌정맥혈전증에서 직접작용 항응고제를 쓴 쪽의 큰 출혈이 1.2%, 표준 치료가 2.4% 로 줄었지만 통계로 뚜렷하지는 않았습니다.
evidence.population: Current guidelines recommend the standard-of-care anticoagulation (vitamin K antagonists or low-molecular-weight heparin) in patients with cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT). | Herein, we performed a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) to assess the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) compared with the current standard of care in patients with CVT.

evidence.title: Non-immunosuppressive treatment for IgA nephropathy.
evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_16: Compared to placebo or no treatment, renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibition probably decreases proteinuria (3 studies, 199 participants: MD - 0.71 g/24 h, 95% CI -1.04 to -0.39; moderate certainty evidence) but may result in little or no difference to kidney failure or doubling of serum creatinine (SCr), or complete remission of proteinuria (low certainty evidence).
evidence.outcome: We aimed to examine all non-immunosuppressive therapies (e.g. anticoagulants, antihypertensives, dietary restriction and supplementation, tonsillectomy, and herbal medicines) in the management of IgAN. | The risk of adverse events may be no different with RAS inhibition compared to either placebo or symptomatic treatment (low certainty evidence). | Anticoagulant therapy, fish oil, and traditional Chinese medicines exhibited small benefits to kidney function in patients with IgAN when compared to placebo or no treatment.
evidence.key_finding: Compared to placebo or no treatment, renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibition probably decreases proteinuria (3 studies, 199 participants: MD - 0.71 g/24 h, 95% CI -1.04 to -0.39; moderate certainty evidence) but may result in little or no difference to kidney failure or doubling of serum creatinine (SCr), or complete remission of proteinuria (low certainty evidence).
evidence.key_finding_ko: 레닌안지오텐신계 억제제를 쓴 쪽에서 단백뇨가 줄었지만(3개 연구, 199명), 신부전이나 혈청 크레아티닌 배가에서는 차이가 뚜렷하지 않았습니다.
evidence.population: We aimed to examine all non-immunosuppressive therapies (e.g. anticoagulants, antihypertensives, dietary restriction and supplementation, tonsillectomy, and herbal medicines) in the management of IgAN. | Anticoagulant therapy, fish oil, and traditional Chinese medicines exhibited small benefits to kidney function in patients with IgAN when compared to placebo or no treatment.

all_evidence.title: Prediction of major and clinically relevant bleeding in patients with VTE treated with edoxaban or vitamin K antagonists.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: Significant risk factors for major bleeding during edoxaban treatment were female sex, concomitant antiplatelet therapy, haemoglobin ≤10 g/dl, history of arterial hypertension, and systolic blood pressure >160 mmHg.
all_evidence.outcome: Better understanding of risk factors for major bleeding events during anticoagulant treatment for venous thromboembolism (VTE) may help physicians when deciding on intensity and duration of treatment. | The primary aim of this study was to identify risk factors for major and clinically relevant bleeding in patients receiving the oral factor Xa inhibitor edoxaban or warfarin for the treatment of acute VTE. | Bleeding risk factors were evaluated in 4118 patients who received edoxaban and significant variables were combined in a prediction model.
all_evidence.key_finding: Significant risk factors for major bleeding during edoxaban treatment were female sex, concomitant antiplatelet therapy, haemoglobin ≤10 g/dl, history of arterial hypertension, and systolic blood pressure >160 mmHg.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 에독사반을 먹는 동안 큰 출혈 위험이 높았던 조건은 여성, 항혈소판제 병용, 헤모글로빈 10 g/dl 이하, 고혈압, 수축기혈압 160 초과였습니다.
all_evidence.publication_types: Clinical Trial, Phase III|Comparative Study|Journal Article|Multicenter Study|Randomized Controlled Trial|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

all_evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants combined with antiplatelet drugs for patients with peripheral artery disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: Compared with antiplatelet drugs alone, NOACs combined with antiplatelet drugs resulted in lower risk of ischemic stroke events (OR = 0.75, 95%CI 0.57-0.98, p = 0.03), while other treatment effects were not worse than those of single antiplatelet drugs (p ≥ 0.05).
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: The efficacy and safety of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs) combined with antiplatelet drugs in patients with peripheral artery disease remain largely unknown. | OBJECTIVE: The aim of this meta-analysis was to explore the effects of NOACs combined with antiplatelet drugs versus antiplatelet drugs alone in this population. | According to the I2 statistic, a random or fixed-effect model was used to analyze the safety and effectiveness of NOACs combined with antiplatelet drugs in peripheral artery disease patients.
all_evidence.key_finding: Compared with antiplatelet drugs alone, NOACs combined with antiplatelet drugs resulted in lower risk of ischemic stroke events (OR = 0.75, 95%CI 0.57-0.98, p = 0.03), while other treatment effects were not worse than those of single antiplatelet drugs (p ≥ 0.05).

all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: The efficacy and safety of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs) combined with antiplatelet drugs in patients with peripheral artery disease remain largely unknown.

all_evidence.title: An Updated Meta-Analysis of DOACs vs. VKAs in Atrial Fibrillation Patients With Bioprosthetic Heart Valve.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: In terms of the safety outcomes, DOACs was associated with lower risks of major bleeding (RR = 0.70, 95%CI: 0.59-0.82) and intracranial bleeding (RR = 0.42, 95%CI: 0.26-0.70), but the risks of any bleeding (RR = 0.85, 95%CI: 0.65-1.13) and gastrointestinal bleeding (RR = 0.92, 95%CI: 0.73-1.17) are not significantly different when compared with VKAs.
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend the utilization of direct-acting oral anticoagulants (DOACs) in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (AF). | However, the optimal anticoagulation strategy for AF patients with bioprosthetic heart valves (BPHV) remains controversial. | In terms of the safety outcomes, DOACs was associated with lower risks of major bleeding (RR = 0.70, 95%CI: 0.59-0.82) and intracranial bleeding (RR = 0.42, 95%CI: 0.26-0.70), but the risks of any bleeding (RR = 0.85, 95%CI: 0.65-1.13) and gastrointestinal bleeding (RR = 0.92, 95%CI: 0.73-1.17) are not significantly different when compared with VKAs.
all_evidence.key_finding: In terms of the safety outcomes, DOACs was associated with lower risks of major bleeding (RR = 0.70, 95%CI: 0.59-0.82) and intracranial bleeding (RR = 0.42, 95%CI: 0.26-0.70), but the risks of any bleeding (RR = 0.85, 95%CI: 0.65-1.13) and gastrointestinal bleeding (RR = 0.92, 95%CI: 0.73-1.17) are not significantly different when compared with VKAs.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 직접작용 항응고제를 쓴 쪽에서 큰 출혈(0.70)과 뇌출혈(0.42) 위험이 낮았지만, 전체 출혈과 위장관 출혈은 차이가 없었습니다.
all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend the utilization of direct-acting oral anticoagulants (DOACs) in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (AF). | However, the optimal anticoagulation strategy for AF patients with bioprosthetic heart valves (BPHV) remains controversial.

all_evidence.title: Clinical safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of the novel factor Xa inhibitor DY-807f in healthy volunteers.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: RESULTS: DY-807f doses were safe and well-tolerated with no dose-dependent increase in adverse events up to 360 mg.
all_evidence.outcome: INTRODUCTION: Since Vitamin K antagonists are associated with various limitations such as narrow therapeutic window, slow onset and offset of effect, and numerous interactions with food and drugs, new oral anticoagulants targeted to inhibit thrombin or factor Xa (FXa) have been developed. | RESULTS: DY-807f doses were safe and well-tolerated with no dose-dependent increase in adverse events up to 360 mg. | Coagulation parameters (Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT) and Prothrombin Time (PT)) were linearly correlated with plasma DY-807 (free base of DY-807f) concentrations (correlation coefficient: 0.786 for aPTT, 0.945 for PT).
all_evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: DY-807f doses were safe and well-tolerated with no dose-dependent increase in adverse events up to 360 mg.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: DY-807f 는 360 mg 까지 용량을 올려도 이상반응이 늘지 않았고 잘 견뎠습니다.

all_evidence.title: Phase 1 study of the effect of icosapent ethyl on warfarin pharmacokinetic and anticoagulation parameters.
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: CONCLUSIONS: IPE 4 g/day did not significantly change the single-dose AUC(0-∞) or C(max) of R- and S-warfarin or the anticoagulation pharmacodynamics of warfarin when co-administered as racemic warfarin at 25 mg.
all_evidence.outcome: EPA, the active metabolite of IPE, is mainly metabolized via β-oxidation, and studies suggest that omega-3 fatty acids such as EPA may have antithrombotic effects. | The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of IPE on the pharmacokinetic and anticoagulation pharmacodynamics of warfarin, a substrate of cytochrome P450 2C9-mediated metabolism. | Primary pharmacokinetic end points were area under the concentration-versus-time curve from zero to infinity (AUC(0-∞)) and maximum plasma concentration (C(max)) for R- and S-warfarin; pharmacodynamic end points were area under the international normalized ratio (INR) effect-time curve after the warfarin dose (AUC(INR)) and maximum INR (INR(max)).
all_evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSIONS: IPE 4 g/day did not significantly change the single-dose AUC(0-∞) or C(max) of R- and S-warfarin or the anticoagulation pharmacodynamics of warfarin when co-administered as racemic warfarin at 25 mg.

all_evidence.outcome: Better understanding of risk factors for major bleeding events during anticoagulant treatment for venous thromboembolism (VTE) may help physicians when deciding on intensity and duration of treatment. | The primary aim of this study was to identify risk factors for major and clinically relevant bleeding in patients receiving the oral factor Xa inhibitor edoxaban or warfarin for the treatment of acute VTE. | Bleeding risk factors were evaluated in 4118 patients who received edoxaban and significant variables were combined in a prediction model.
all_evidence.key_finding: Significant risk factors for major bleeding during edoxaban treatment were female sex, concomitant antiplatelet therapy, haemoglobin ≤10 g/dl, history of arterial hypertension, and systolic blood pressure >160 mmHg.

evidence.title: Deterioration of renal function is delayed in patients with atrial fibrillation treated with direct oral anticoagulants compared to vitamin K antagonists: systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_7: DOACs were associated with a lower risk of ≥30 % eGFR decline (HR:0.72, 95 %CI:0.59-0.88), progression to stage five CKD (HR:0.49,95 %CI:0.37-0.64) and doubling of serum creatinine (HR:0.50, 95 %CI:0.42-0.61). ≥30 % eGFR decline was also lower when apixaban, dabigatran and rivaroxaban were compared separately to VKAs, (HR:0.81, 95 %CI:0.69-0.95), (HR:0.61, 95 %CI:0.48-0.78) and (HR:0.80, 95 %CI:0.70-0.92) respectively.
evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: The use of anticoagulants has been linked to anticoagulant-related nephropathy, a condition initially reported in patients treated with warfarin. | However, cases have also been documented in patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs).
evidence.key_finding: DOACs were associated with a lower risk of ≥30 % eGFR decline (HR:0.72, 95 %CI:0.59-0.88), progression to stage five CKD (HR:0.49,95 %CI:0.37-0.64) and doubling of serum creatinine (HR:0.50, 95 %CI:0.42-0.61). ≥30 % eGFR decline was also lower when apixaban, dabigatran and rivaroxaban were compared separately to VKAs, (HR:0.81, 95 %CI:0.69-0.95), (HR:0.61, 95 %CI:0.48-0.78) and (HR:0.80, 95 %CI:0.70-0.92) respectively.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 직접작용 항응고제를 쓴 쪽에서 콩팥 기능이 30% 넘게 낮아질 위험이 적었습니다(위험비 0.72).
evidence.population: BACKGROUND: The use of anticoagulants has been linked to anticoagulant-related nephropathy, a condition initially reported in patients treated with warfarin. | However, cases have also been documented in patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). | DOACs were associated with a lower risk of ≥30 % eGFR decline (HR:0.72, 95 %CI:0.59-0.88), progression to stage five CKD (HR:0.49,95 %CI:0.37-0.64) and doubling of serum creatinine (HR:0.50, 95 %CI:0.42-0.61). ≥30 % eGFR decline was also lower when apixaban, dabigatran and rivaroxaban were compared separately to VKAs, (HR:0.81, 95 %CI:0.69-0.95), (HR:0.61, 95 %CI:0.48-0.78) and (HR:0.80, 95 %CI:0.70-0.92) respectively.

evidence.title: Non-immunosuppressive treatment for IgA nephropathy.
evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_16: Compared to placebo or no treatment, renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibition probably decreases proteinuria (3 studies, 199 participants: MD - 0.71 g/24 h, 95% CI -1.04 to -0.39; moderate certainty evidence) but may result in little or no difference to kidney failure or doubling of serum creatinine (SCr), or complete remission of proteinuria (low certainty evidence).
evidence.outcome: We aimed to examine all non-immunosuppressive therapies (e.g. anticoagulants, antihypertensives, dietary restriction and supplementation, tonsillectomy, and herbal medicines) in the management of IgAN. | The risk of adverse events may be no different with RAS inhibition compared to either placebo or symptomatic treatment (low certainty evidence). | Anticoagulant therapy, fish oil, and traditional Chinese medicines exhibited small benefits to kidney function in patients with IgAN when compared to placebo or no treatment.
evidence.key_finding: Compared to placebo or no treatment, renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibition probably decreases proteinuria (3 studies, 199 participants: MD - 0.71 g/24 h, 95% CI -1.04 to -0.39; moderate certainty evidence) but may result in little or no difference to kidney failure or doubling of serum creatinine (SCr), or complete remission of proteinuria (low certainty evidence).
evidence.key_finding_ko: 레닌안지오텐신계 억제제를 쓴 쪽에서 단백뇨가 줄었지만(3개 연구, 199명), 신부전이나 혈청 크레아티닌 배가에서는 차이가 뚜렷하지 않았습니다.
evidence.population: We aimed to examine all non-immunosuppressive therapies (e.g. anticoagulants, antihypertensives, dietary restriction and supplementation, tonsillectomy, and herbal medicines) in the management of IgAN. | Anticoagulant therapy, fish oil, and traditional Chinese medicines exhibited small benefits to kidney function in patients with IgAN when compared to placebo or no treatment.

evidence.title: Fatal intracranial haemorrhage occurring after oral anticoagulant treatment initiation for secondary stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation.
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: CONCLUSIONS: Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants for intracranial haemorrhages and VKA-ICH occurring during secondary stroke prevention of AF patients have comparable baseline characteristics and outcomes except for the risk of fatal ICH within 30 days, which might be greater in VKA-ICH.
evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: In this pooled analysis of seven multicentre cohorts potential differences were investigated in the incidence, characteristics and outcomes between intracranial haemorrhages (ICHs) associated with the use of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOAC-ICH) or with vitamin K antagonists (VKA-ICH) in ischaemic stroke patients after oral anticoagulant treatment initiation for atrial fibrillation (AF). | CONCLUSIONS: Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants for intracranial haemorrhages and VKA-ICH occurring during secondary stroke prevention of AF patients have comparable baseline characteristics and outcomes except for the risk of fatal ICH within 30 days, which might be greater in VKA-ICH.
evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSIONS: Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants for intracranial haemorrhages and VKA-ICH occurring during secondary stroke prevention of AF patients have comparable baseline characteristics and outcomes except for the risk of fatal ICH within 30 days, which might be greater in VKA-ICH.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 심방세동 환자의 뇌출혈에서 결과는 대체로 비슷했지만, 30일 안의 치명적 뇌출혈 위험은 비타민 K 길항제 쪽이 더 높을 수 있습니다.

evidence.title: Cost-Effectiveness of First-Line Sevelamer and Lanthanum versus Calcium-Based Binders for Hyperphosphatemia of Chronic Kidney Disease.
evidence.venue: Value in health : the journal of the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: Sensitivity analyses were conducted for risk pooling methods, omission of dialysis costs, and persistence of drug effects on mortality.
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity analyses were conducted for risk pooling methods, omission of dialysis costs, and persistence of drug effects on mortality.
evidence.key_finding: Sensitivity analyses were conducted for risk pooling methods, omission of dialysis costs, and persistence of drug effects on mortality.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 위험을 합산하는 방식, 투석 비용을 뺀 경우, 약효가 이어지는 기간을 바꿔 가며 사망에 대한 민감도 분석을 했습니다.
evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Phosphate binders are used to treat hyperphosphatemia among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). | OBJECTIVES: To conduct an economic evaluation comparing calcium-free binders sevelamer and lanthanum with calcium-based binders for patients with CKD. | A Markov model consisting of non-dialysis-dependent (NDD)-CKD, dialysis-dependent (DD)-CKD, and death was developed to estimate the incremental costs and effects of sevelamer and lanthanum versus those of calcium-based binders.

evidence.title: Vitamin D status and intermediate vascular and bone outcomes in chronic kidney disease: a secondary post hoc analysis of IMPROVE-CKD.
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: Those with 25(OH)D deficiency were more likely to have diabetes (56% vs 38%), cardiovascular disease (54% vs 36%) and lower serum calcium (2.29 ± 0.13 vs 2.34 ± 0.13 mmol/L).
evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and has been associated with abnormalities of mineral metabolism and vascular calcification. | Those with 25(OH)D deficiency were more likely to have diabetes (56% vs 38%), cardiovascular disease (54% vs 36%) and lower serum calcium (2.29 ± 0.13 vs 2.34 ± 0.13 mmol/L).
evidence.key_finding: Those with 25(OH)D deficiency were more likely to have diabetes (56% vs 38%), cardiovascular disease (54% vs 36%) and lower serum calcium (2.29 ± 0.13 vs 2.34 ± 0.13 mmol/L).
evidence.key_finding_ko: 비타민 D 가 모자란 쪽에 당뇨병(56% 대 38%)과 심혈관질환(54% 대 36%)이 더 흔했고, 혈중 칼슘은 낮았습니다.
evidence.population: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and has been associated with abnormalities of mineral metabolism and vascular calcification. | We aimed to test our hypothesis that vitamin D deficiency is associated with arterial stiffness, aortic calcification and lower bone mineral density (BMD) in patients with CKD. | METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis was performed using baseline data from the IMpact of Phosphate Reduction On Vascular Endpoints in CKD (IMPROVE-CKD) study cohort.

evidence.title: Vitamin D status and mortality risk among patients on dialysis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
evidence.venue: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: CONCLUSIONS: In the present study, increased serum 25(OH)D level was significantly associated with lower all-cause mortality and lower cardiovascular mortality in dialysis patients.
evidence.outcome: Although vitamin D deficiency is closely associated with cardiovascular disease (CVD) and high mortality in the general population, the relationship between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in dialysis patients is uncertain. | We aim to explore the relationship between serum 25(OH)D levels and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in dialysis patients. | We did a systematic literature search in PubMed and Embase to identify studies reporting the relationship between serum 25(OH)D levels and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients on dialysis.
evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSIONS: In the present study, increased serum 25(OH)D level was significantly associated with lower all-cause mortality and lower cardiovascular mortality in dialysis patients.

evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Meta-Analysis|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't|Systematic Review
